'Together, Let us Love, Encourage, Achieve and Flourish'
Our next Family Service is 9am on Monday 16th November at Crowcombe Church. This will be followed by our Autumn Term Parent Forum - we do hope you can join us.
Crowcombe & Stogumber Federated C of E Primary Schools are situated at the foot of the Quantock Hills, an area of outstanding beauty, deep in rural Somerset. We are proud of our Christian distinctiveness which is encompassed in our theologically rooted school vision which underpins all aspects of school life.
Our school community is based on a foundation of generosity, optimism, determination, curiosity and courage. We are driven by high standards and an enthusiastic love of learning, within a positive Christian ethos.
We share an Executive Headteacher, a governing body and a PTA. This enables us to offer extended opportunities to our children with a wider range of activities and staff expertise. We have our own mini-bus which is used on a daily basis to provide free transport between the schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crowcombe CE VA & Stogumber CE VC Primary Schools - Church Distinctiveness including SIAMS report
pageCache.text:
Church Distinctiveness including SIAMS report
Together, Let us Love, Encourage, Achieve and Flourish
Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) Reports
Our Collective Worship Ambassadors
Our collective worship ambassadors are a group of children who help plan and lead collective worship across the schools.
Our Core Christian Values
To bring our school vision to life, we have discerned five christian values which will guide the way that we do things in our two schools. A Value is a principle that guides our thinking and our behaviour. At Crowcombe and Stogumber, every individual is valued for who they are and what they contribute to the school. Values are intended to support the personal, social and spiritual development of every pupil throughout the school.
Our 5 core values are:
Generosity Optimism Determination Courage Curiosity
When we think about generosity we usually think about being generous with money or possessions. However, at Crowcombe and Stogumber we can also be generous with our time, our gifts and our abilities. Generous people often say that they receive much more than they give. Perhaps this is because when someone is generous to us, it makes us want to be generous in return.
God’s generosity is best described as ‘grace’, love given freely without limit or conditions. This generosity, once experienced and acknowledged by an individual, can in turn release a generous spirit towards others.
At Crowcombe and Stogumber we believe that optimism doesn't mean pretending life is always wonderful. Optimism means embracing reality. Through maintaining a positive outlook we accept that there will be bad days, but also many good days. When we are grounded in reality, we know where we are and how far we need to go. Once we know how far our goal may be from where we are, optimism can give us the motivation to make plans to get to where we want to go.
In the Bible another suitable term for optimism is hope. Optimism leads to resilience and God suggests “And not only that, but we also glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces perseverance; and perseverance, character; and character, hope” (Romans 5:3-4). Here we see that perseverance and resilience leads to hope (optimism).
At Crowcombe and Stogumber we believe that Determination means not giving up when things get difficult. Determination is being able to do or achieve something. It is about making your mind up about something and driving on to achieve a goal. When we talk about teaching children hard work and determination, we’re talking about building their self-confidence and self-image to pursue their dreams, achieve the goals they set out to achieve, and to have the chance to “stay on track” even when something is difficult. In our schools teaching determination means offering children the chance to try new things, encouraging them to not be afraid to make mistakes, helping them problem solve when they hit a difficulty, and offering specific and effort-oriented praise.
In the Bible it states “Let us run with determination the race that lies before us” (Hebrews 12:1). Jesus frequently encouraged his disciples to ‘endure patiently’ the difficulties and obstacles they encountered and to persevere in the face of adversity. He himself trusted in God even when his enemies tried to stop his work and plotted his death.
At our schools courage is more than being brave – it is demonstrating an inner confidence about ones self and what is important. It is having the confidence to do something challenging be it facing a fear or phobia or choosing to stand up for others, even if it makes you unpopular. At Crowcombe and Stogumber we try to encourage the children to stand firm by their own faith, beliefs or courage of conviction. Being able to make up your own mind and not be swayed by pressure from others is an important life skill that will stand our children in good stead as they move on from us at the end of Year 6.
Courage is a core value for our church school because God asks us to be brave in the face of hardship. In the book of Joshua, God tells his people to ‘Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened, for the Lord God is with you wherever you go.’ This reminds us to stand against injustice and to be the best we can be when things are difficult.
At Crowcombe and Stogumber we kindle the spark of curiosity in our pupils by teaching a creative and broad curriculum which inspires, engages and motivates learners. Our children experience extraordinary learning opportunities through a range of visitors, workshops, trips and lessons to inspire intellectual curiosity. Our teachers are passionate about learning and foster inquisitiveness and empower our pupils with the skills to explore the world around them.
As a Church school, curiosity opens our heart and mind to the Spirit. As the apostle Paul says in 2 Corinthians 3:17, “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.” The curious mind creates deep thinkers and confident communicators; we encourage questioning, reasoning, debate and justification.
Our school values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.
As a Church of England School, our Christian Values underpin all that we do. Every week we focus on a specific value in order to gain a better understanding of how these values impact the way that we live. The values are displayed around our school and in all of our classrooms and are regularly referred to in order to help the children fully understand what they mean and how they link to their own lives. Our Collective Worships link closely to the weekly value and provides further opportunity for learning, reflection and application.
Our values are the foundations of our behaviour policy, and we use them to talk to the children about their actions, to help them understand consequences. This then helps them to make changes and choices to ensure they are following our values within school and in their own lives at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crowcombe CE VA & Stogumber CE VC Primary Schools - Collective Worship Ambassadors
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship Ambassadors
As part of each of our family services the children write prayers. The Year 6 children wrote the following prayers as part of our end of year service.
We gather here today to celebrate the last day of term.
We thank you for all the years at this school. Thank you for our memories. Thank you for our teachers that we had on the way and thank you for the stuff we learnt on the way.
Please bless us for the future - for all the good and all the bad, all the hard and easy times, all the times we feel down and all the we happy ask for you to bless us.
Grant us wisdom in the years ahead, grant us courage when we are faced with wrong, give us strength when we need to make things right. Give us support when we need to choose between good and bad.
We pray for parents and teachers and brothers and sisters and uncles and aunties and cousins and so on - may they be blessed with strength and wisdom.
In your holy name, we pray, Amen.
As we assemble here today, our hearts open up to your love and fill with gratitude as we close the curtain on our years at this school.
Thank you for supporting us throughout our journey at Crowcombe and Stogumber Primary Schools. We thank you for helping us through the highs and lows of our years here. Due to your love and care, we have created many wonderful friendships and met many marvellous people along the way. We are grateful for the enjoyable moments and opportunities that we have shared with all of our friends and family. Thank you for all the challenges which have helped us thrive and bring to light our unique gifts and talents.
As we prepare to depart from this unforgettable school, we ask for your blessing to give us strength for the years ahead. May you direct us in our new schools, help us to generate new friendships, and give us courage to welcome more challenges for the future with confidence and faith.
Grant us wisdom in our commitments, tolerance in our difficulties, and happiness in our achievements. May we remember our core values in ourselves, and carry them along with us for our path ahead. May we be kind, respectful and determined as we take the next step to a brighter education.
We pray for our teachers, classmates and families that have assisted us along the way. Please continue to bless them with stability and passion.
As we say farewell, our hearts will be full of desire and enthusiasm. Thank you for aiding us on this journey and may you watch over us and help us make a positive impact on the world.
In Jesus’s name we pray, Amen.
Dear Heavenly Father,
As we gather here today, we come before you with hearts full of thanks and anticipation.
We thank you for helping us through the wonderful years we have spent at this school. Thank you for helping us learn and grow, for the teachers who have supported us, and for the opportunities to discover our gifts and talents.
As we prepare to leave this school and move on to new experiences and adventures, We ask for your blessing on all of us here today. Help us continue on our learning journey, Help us to make new friends and give us courage to embrace new challenges with confidence.
Please grant us wisdom in our decisions, patience through our struggles and happiness in our triumph. Help us to think back to the values and lessons we have mastered and carry them with us always. May we always be kind, respectful and may we strive to make a positive impact in our learning.
We pray for our teachers, our classmates and families who have all supported us along the way. May they continue to be blessed with happiness and love. As we say goodbye, we do so with hearts full joy and excitement for the future. Thank you for being with us on part of the journey, and please continue to watch over us as we carry on throughout the years to come.
In your holy name, we pray, Amen.
As we meet today, we gather before you with hearts full of gratitude and anticipation.
We thank you for the many happy times we have spent together at this school. Thank you for the friends we have made, the teachers who have taught us, and the lessons we have learned from.
As we prepare to go onto our new schools, we ask for your help. May you guide us as we leave this school, and help us make new friends at our new schools.
May you give us guidance as we embark on our journey to fresh starts at our new schools. Help us remember the times we have gathered together to learn and to have fun.
We pray here today for our teachers, classmates, and families who helped us along the way. As we go on we say goodbye with hearts full of hope and thanks.
Children
Collective Worship Ambassadors

pageCache.pageTitle: Crowcombe CE VA & Stogumber CE VC Primary Schools - Our  School Christian Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our School Christian Vision and Values
Together, Let us Love, Encourage, Achieve and Flourish
Our school vision is theologically rooted and underpins and is interwoven into all aspect of school life. It is through this vision that we model our school culture, values and ethos. Our school vision drives our work and enables the schools to live up to their foundations as church schools. It reflects the needs of the schools and communities and through embedding and living out this vision we hope to deepen the relationship between the schools, families, churches and communities.
The purpose of our school vision is to lay out Who we are; Why we are here; and therefore How we live our lives. When exploring this we considered our 5 core valves:
Generosity Optimism Determination Curiosity Courage
We also explored what is special about us 'Crowcombe and Stogumber C of E Primary Schools' and the importance we place on being together and ensuring everyone in our schools and communities feel valued, included and that they belong. During our exploration we found a passage from the old testament that reflected our core message.
'And let us consider how we may spur one another on towards love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together, as some as are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another - and all the more as you see the day approaching'
This resonated with us and highlighted key words that we believe reflect our vision for the schools. These words formed our vision:
Together, Let us Love, Encourage, Achieve and Flourish
We actively explore these words with the children through classroom teaching and collective worship. We explore the importance of us being together through friendship, and of showing love and generosity by loving our neighbour as ourselves. We explore encouraging others as well as persevering ourselves and showing determination. We explore having the courage and curiosity to achieve throughout all aspects of our lives, and how with optimism we can all flourish together.
We hope all of our pupils, staff, governors, families and wider communities will support and join us in embedding our school vision.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crowcombe CE VA & Stogumber CE VC Primary Schools - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to Crowcombe C of E VA & Stogumber C of E VC Primary Schools.
Nestled at the foot of the beautiful Quantock Hills in rural Somerset, Crowcombe and Stogumber Federated Church of England Primary Schools are vibrant, nurturing learning communities where every child is valued, supported and encouraged to flourish. We are proud of our Christian distinctiveness, which is encompassed in our theologically rooted school vision and underpins all aspects of school life.
'Together, Let us Love, Encourage, Achieve and Flourish'
Our Christian vision shapes our relationships, our curriculum, and our commitment to ensuring that every member of our school community feels a true sense of belonging. Guided by this vision, we foster a culture of generosity, optimism, determination, curiosity and courage, where children are inspired to grow academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually.
We are committed to being truly inclusive schools. We believe that every child is unique and has the right to feel safe, respected and valued. Through high-quality teaching, personalised support and strong partnerships with families, we work to remove barriers to learning and provide equitable opportunities for all children, regardless of background, ability, need or circumstance. Our aim is for every child to achieve their full potential and to thrive as confident, compassionate and successful individuals.
As a federation, we share an Executive Headteacher, Governing Body and PTA, enabling us to offer a wide range of experiences, expertise and opportunities across both schools. Our dedicated mini-bus provides daily transport between sites, strengthening our sense of one school family.
As a small school federation, we regularly review our organisational structure to ensure we are providing the very best educational experience for all children. For the 2026-2027 academic year, Reception and Year 1 pupils, from both school rolls, will be taught at Stogumber School, while Year 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 pupils, from both school rolls, will be educated at Crowcombe School.
Although we are based across two sites, we see ourselves as one school community, united by our shared vision, values and commitment to providing exceptional opportunities for every child. We work closely together across both sites, with children benefiting from regular shared learning experiences, collective worship, celebrations, educational visits, sporting events, performances and enrichment activities. This collaborative approach enables our children to develop strong relationships across year groups, fosters a sense of belonging, and ensures that every pupil feels part of our wider school family.
Our small class sizes and high staff-to-pupil ratios allow us to know every child as an individual and provide the support, challenge and encouragement they need to achieve their full potential and flourish.
Above all, our schools are places where children are loved, encouraged to believe in themselves, inspired to achieve their very best, and supported to flourish within a caring and inclusive Christian community. We are proud of the kindness, respect and sense of responsibility shown by our pupils, and of the strong partnerships we build with families and the wider community.
Together, we create a place where everyone belongs, everyone matters, and everyone can flourish.
Please do not hesitate to contact us should you require any further information about the schools.
Executive Headteacher

pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
PHYSICAL EDUCATION PROVISION AND EXPENDITURE OF SCHOOL SPORTS FUNDING
Please read the information below for details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we use this funding to enhance opportunities for all pupils.
At Crowcombe and Stogumber C of E Primary Schools, effective, enjoyable and inclusive Physical Education lies at the heart of our curriculum. We are committed to developing healthy, active bodies and minds, and recognise the vital role that PE and Learning Outside the Classroom (LOtC) play in supporting children's physical, emotional and social development.
Our pupils benefit from a wide range of opportunities to be active throughout the school day. These include daily physical activity, leadership opportunities for older pupils, outdoor learning experiences, high-quality PE lessons, and a variety of extra-curricular clubs and competitive sporting events. We believe that every child should be encouraged to develop confidence, resilience, teamwork and a lifelong love of physical activity.
As a small rural school, participation in local sports festivals, competitions and tournaments provides invaluable opportunities for our pupils to broaden their experiences, meet and compete alongside children from other schools, and develop their sporting skills in a wider context. Thanks to the support of our staff, families and the PE and Sport Premium funding, we are able to offer a broad programme of sporting opportunities.
We are proud that our commitment to high-quality PE, school sport and physical activity has been recognised nationally through the Gold School Games Award, achieved in July 2026. This prestigious award reflects our dedication to providing inclusive, engaging and accessible sporting opportunities for all pupils, while promoting participation, leadership and personal development through sport.
A significant contribution to this success comes from our Year 6 Young Leaders, who organise and lead lunchtime activities for Key Stage 2 pupils, support younger children in developing their skills and confidence, and help to plan and deliver house competitions and sporting events throughout the year. Their enthusiasm and leadership play a key role in fostering a positive sporting culture across the school.

SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities)
What Inclusion means to us:
At our schools, inclusion means that every child is valued, supported, and given the opportunity to succeed. We are committed to creating an environment where all children can learn, grow, and take part fully in school life.
Our vision, “Together let us love, encourage, achieve and flourish,” is at the heart of our inclusive ethos.
Inclusion at our school means working together – with pupils, families, staff, and external professionals – to ensure that every child feels they belong and can flourish as part of our learning community.
Our SENDCo & Senior Mental Health Lead is Mrs Carter.
Mrs Carter can be contacted at Crowcombe and Stogumber Primary School either by phone or email.
Please call: 01984 618273 or01984 656311 Email: crowcombeoffice@crowstog.co.uk
Mrs Carter works on a Monday and Tuesday.
Our Inclusion governor is Mrs Dean.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crowcombe CE VA & Stogumber CE VC Primary Schools - Climate Ambassadors
pageCache.text:
Climate Ambassadors
We are excited to introduce our three Climate Ambassador groups, who will play an important role in helping our school develop and lead positive action to support sustainability.
The Biodiversity team will focus on protecting and enhancing the natural habitats around our school, finding ways to encourage wildlife and increase awareness of the importance of caring for our environment. The Community Garden group will help to develop and maintain our growing spaces, promoting healthy living and a shared sense of responsibility for our outdoor areas. Finally, the Waste team will work to reduce, reuse, and recycle more effectively across the school, encouraging everyone to make thoughtful choices about the resources we use.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crowcombe CE VA & Stogumber CE VC Primary Schools - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our Curriculum
At Crowcombe and Stogumber C of E Primary Schools we provide a rich and diverse curriculum that is coherently planned and sequenced to enable progression and build on pupil knowledge and understanding with key concepts woven throughout. Throughout our curriculum we embed our school vision ' Together, Let us Love, Encourage, Achieve and Flourish'.
We work in mixed aged classes and have a two year rolling programme for children in KS1, Lower KS2 and Upper KS2.
We value all curriculum subjects and have carefully planned and sequenced an ambitious curriculum for each subject area, considering what we teach, why we teach it and how it builds on prior knowledge and provides the foundations for later learning.
Our curriculum offer is fully inclusive and accessible to all, regardless of background or ability. We celebrate diversity and promote equality, providing opportunities for all learners to engage, participate, and thrive.
Each area of the curriculum is led by a member of our teaching staff who ensure that the intent of their curriculum area is well sequenced, planned and resourced and that teacher's have good knowledge to effectively implement the curriculum to ensure the pupils develop the knowledge and skills to achieve well.
Our Subject Leader are:
Mrs Mason - EYFS and KS1 Leader; English & Maths Lead for EYFS and KS1
Miss Martin - KS2 Lead; English and Maths Lead for KS2, MFL
Mrs Carter - SENDCo, Personal, Social, Health and Relationships Education (PSHRE)
Mr Brown - Computing & History
Ms Jolliffe - Religious Education (RE)
Mrs Phillips - Art and Design, and Design and Technology (DT)
Miss Storey - Physical Education (PE)
Mr Wedderkopp - Sustainability Lead, Geography and Learning Outside the Classroom (LOTC)
Please do explore our curriculum offer for each subject below.
If you would like to know more, please contact the school and arrange to talk to the subject lead where they will be very pleased to share with you what the children learn in more detail.
